subject: Biology
central_question: How are major plant groups distinguished by body organisation, pigments, reproduction, vascular tissues, spores, seeds, and life-cycle patterns?
in_scope_units: Changing approaches to plant classification, including artificial, natural, phylogenetic, numerical, cytotaxonomic, and chemotaxonomic systems.
Algae, their organisation, reproduction, economic importance, and the classes Chlorophyceae, Phaeophyceae, and Rhodophyceae.
Bryophytes, their gametophyte-dominant life cycle, water dependence, ecological roles, liverworts, and mosses.
Pteridophytes, vascular sporophytes, prothalli, homospory, heterospory, and the evolutionary significance of seed habit.
Gymnosperms, naked ovules and seeds, cones, reduced gametophytes, pollination, and fertilisation.
Angiosperms as flowering plants with enclosed seeds and their broad division into dicotyledons and monocotyledons.
banned_topics: Detailed morphology and anatomy of flowering-plant organs
Detailed double fertilisation and embryology of angiosperms
Five-kingdom classification outside the limits needed to define Plantae

known_pitfalls.claim: Cyanobacteria are algae within Kingdom Plantae.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter explicitly excludes cyanobacteria from Plantae and treats algae here as eukaryotic plant groups.

known_pitfalls.claim: All algae have the same pigments and stored food.
known_pitfalls.correction: Green, brown, and red algae differ in major pigments, reserve food, wall composition, and flagella.

known_pitfalls.claim: The bryophyte sporophyte is independent and dominant.
known_pitfalls.correction: The haploid gametophyte is dominant, while the sporophyte remains attached to and nutritionally dependent on it.

known_pitfalls.claim: All pteridophytes produce one type of spore.
known_pitfalls.correction: Most are homosporous, but Selaginella and Salvinia are heterosporous.
Gymnosperm ovules and seeds are not enclosed by an ovary wall and remain naked.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Exercise 1: compare algal classes using pigments, reserve food, cell wall, and flagella.
NCERT Exercise 9: distinguish red algae from brown algae and liverworts from mosses.
NCERT Exercise 7: explain heterospory and its evolutionary significance using Selaginella and Salvinia.
NCERT Exercise 6: distinguish gymnosperms from angiosperms despite both producing seeds.
NCERT Exercise 10: match representative genera to algae, mosses, pteridophytes, and gymnosperms.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: Use the end-of-chapter EXERCISES 1–11 for algal classes, life cycles, archegonia, heterospory, seed plants, and gymnosperm characteristics.
